label: late original-phase positions (8th/9th input) of long sequences, token-modulated
explanation: Sparse unit (~1% of steps). About 57% of activation mass falls on the 8th and 9th original inputs (orig_idx 7-8), so it is effectively the last input before <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences. Firing rate there is only ~13-23%, and which input token is present matters: f, k, h, j, s, w and 1 have 2-4x lift. The rest of the mass sits in the early copy phase (recall_idx 2-3, ~26%) and scattered late copy steps, again biased toward the same tokens. Strongest activations come at the final original input of 9-token sequences, often f/s/z. Never fires at t=0-1 and almost never on the delimiter step or in short sequences (L<=5). No single clean predicate: precision stays low because most late-position steps do not fire.
